rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq traces the authority of each Imam’s hadith back through the Imams to the Prophet, whose hadith is God’s own speech.
rows.anchor: سمعنا أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول حديثي حديث أبي وحديث أبي حديث جدي

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet was the closest of creation to God; Gabriel invited him onward at the Mi‘raj to a station no angel or messenger had reached, as near as two bows or nearer.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام وذلك أنه يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أقرب الخلق

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ali ibn al-Husayn describes the Prophet as ascending beyond the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary and reaching the stated nearness to his Lord.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام في حديث طويل أنا ابن من علا فاستعلى فجاز سدرة المنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai says this interpretation of the Prophet’s nearness is found in many reports from the Imams of the Prophet’s family.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد هذا المعنى في كثير من روايات أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa‘id reports that the Prophet approached his Lord during the Night Journey and likened the closeness to a bow brought near its string.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال لما أسري بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم اقترب من ربه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the one who drew near and descended as Muhammad, who drew near to his Lord.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { ثم دنا فتدلى } قال هو محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet’s gloss of the distance as two cubits, or less than two cubits.
rows.anchor: مرفوعا عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله { فكان قاب قوسين أو أدنى } قال

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi explains the revelation to the Prophet as direct, face-to-face speech.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى } قال

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Kazim answers that the Prophet saw God with his heart, not with eyesight, citing the verse that the heart did not deny what it saw.
rows.anchor: إلى محمد بن الفضيل قال سألت أبا الحسن عليه السلام هل رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي عن بعض أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka‘b reports that some Companions asked the Prophet whether he had seen his Lord; the report’s answer continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي عن بعض أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال قالوا يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: In the continuation of the Companions’ question, the Prophet says he reached the Lote Tree, whose leaf shaded a community, and was as near to his Lord as two bows or closer.
rows.anchor: انتهيت إلى سدرة المنتهى وإذا الورقة منها تظل أمة من الأمم فكنت من ربي كقاب قوسين أو أدنى

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet describing Sidra berries as locusts and leaves as elephant ears; when God’s command covered it, it changed into ruby, emerald, and similar things.
rows.anchor: أخرج أحمد وابن جرير عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a report from Abu Ja‘far, Gabriel stops at Sidra, tells the Prophet to proceed to a station no creature reached before, and the Prophet sees divine light while majesty intervenes between him and God.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث طويل فلما انتهى به إلى سدرة المنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai explains al-sabha as majesty: it signifies God’s transcendence from creation and therefore points back to that primary sense.
rows.anchor: السبحة الجلال كما فسر في الرواية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report’s conclusion means that the Prophet saw his Lord through the vision of God’s signs.
rows.anchor: ومحصل ذيل الرواية أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم رأى ربه برؤية آياته

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi places the second vision at Sidra in the seventh heaven.
rows.anchor: في قوله تعالى { ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى عند سدرة المنتهى } قال في السماء السابعة

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi says God’s light covered the Lote Tree when the veil between Him and the Messenger was lifted.
rows.anchor: قال لما رفع الحجاب بينه وبين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم غشي نوره السدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai directs readers to his earlier account of the Mi‘raj reports in the opening commentary on Surat al-Isra, where he reviewed their differing descriptions.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في أول تفسير سورة الإسراء روايات جامعة لقصة معراجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier discussion recorded disagreement over whether the Mi‘raj occurred in a dream or while awake, and whether an awake ascent involved body and soul or the soul alone.
rows.anchor: الاختلاف في كيفية معراجه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه كان في المنام أو في اليقظة

rows.speaker: صاحب المناقب
rows.claim: The Sahib al-Manaqib says the Imamis hold that the journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque occurred in body and soul, as the Isra verse indicates.
rows.anchor: عن صاحب المناقب أن الإمامية ترى أن إسراءه من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى كان بالروح والجسم معا

rows.speaker: قوم وكثير من الشيعة
rows.claim: Some say the ascent from Jerusalem to the heavens was in both body and soul; many Shi‘a agree with this view.
rows.anchor: وأما من المسجد الأقصى إلى السماوات فقد قال قوم بكونه بالروح والجسم معا أيضا ووافقهم كثير من الشيعة

rows.speaker: بعض الشيعة وبعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: Some incline to a soul-only ascent from Jerusalem to heaven, and some later scholars also lean toward that position.
rows.anchor: ومال بعضهم إلى كونه بالروح ومال إليه بعض المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai sees no problem with a soul-only ascent if supported by the verses and reports; Sidra’s Garden of Refuge could be the barzakh garden, or the verse could be read consistently with spiritual ascent.
rows.anchor: ولا ضير في القول به لو أيدته القرائن الحافة بالآيات والروايات غير أن من الواجب حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that the Isra occurred in a dream is not one to be considered.
rows.anchor: وأما كون الإسراء في المنام فقد تقدم في تفسير آية الإسراء أنه مما لا ينبغي أن يلتفت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explaining the ascent as night travel to other planets, star systems, or galaxies conflicts with the detailed reports and has no coherent fit with the verses.
rows.anchor: فمما لا يلائمه الأخبار الواردة في تفصيل القصة البتة بل ولا محصل مضامين الآيات المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative in ‘that is their limit of knowledge’ refers to the worldly life discussed in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بذلك إلى أمر الدنيا وهو معلوم من الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The limit of their knowledge is metaphorically its endpoint: knowledge reaches the world as its object, stops there, and does not go beyond it.
rows.anchor: من قبيل الاستعارة كأن العلم يسير إلى المعلوم وينتهي إليه وعلمهم انتهى في مسيره إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because their knowledge stops at worldly life, it becomes their object of desire, concern, and hope; they turn only toward it and find no reassurance beyond it.
rows.anchor: ولازم ذلك أن تكون الدنيا متعلق إرادتهم وطلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assertion that God knows best who strays and who is guided confirms the preceding statement and serves as God’s testimony to it.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لمضمون الجملة السابقة وشهادة منه تعالى عليه

words: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible parsing treats the ownership clause as a circumstantial clause describing the subject of ‘knows best,’ with the waw as circumstantial: God owns the realms, so how could He not know their people?
rows.anchor: والواو للحال، والمعنى إن ربك هو أعلم بالفريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that parsing, ‘so He may recompense’ attaches to the earlier command to turn away: leave their affair to God, who will recompense them and the good-doers.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالظاهر تعلق قوله { ليجزي } الخ، بقوله السابق { فأعرض عمن تولى }

words: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the ownership statement begins a new sentence: turning away from them does not leave them neglected, since God recompenses everyone according to deeds.
rows.anchor: كلاما مستأنفا للدلالة على أن الأمر بالإعراض عنهم لا لإهمالهم وتركهم سدى

words: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit name ‘Allah’ in place of a pronoun conveys the fullness of divine majesty.
rows.anchor: ووضع اسم الجلالة وهو ظاهر موضع الضمير للدلالة على كمال العظمة

words: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership derives from creating and bringing all things into being; it also grounds governance, so the clause implies that both creation and administration belong to Him.
rows.anchor: فالملك ناشىء من الخلق وهو مع ذلك منشأ للتدبير فالجملة دالة على الخلق والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause most clearly makes recompense the goal of God’s creation and governance: evil means disobedience, good means obedience, and the reward is the best recompense; ‘what they did’ may mean deeds or their recompense.
rows.anchor: واللام للغاية، والمعنى له الخلق والتدبير وغاية ذلك

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib explains the root sense of sin as an act that delays a person from reward and good.
rows.anchor: كما ذكره الراغب - الفعل المبطئ عن الثواب والخير

rows.speaker: الرواية
rows.claim: A report defines major sins as those for which God has threatened the Fire.
rows.anchor: كبائر الإثم المعاصي الكبيرة وهو على ما في الرواية ما أوعد الله عليه النار

rows.speaker: أسباب النزول
rows.claim: Reported occasions of revelation describe a Muslim who spent generously in God’s cause, was warned by others that he would become poor and promised they would bear his sins, then stopped spending; these verses were revealed about the incident.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا من المسلمين كان ينفق من ماله في سبيل الله فلامه بعض الناس على كثرة الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story and citations from Moses’ and Abraham’s scriptures clarify the truth against the polytheists’ claim that idols represented God’s daughters, the angels, whom they worshiped for intercession; earlier verses refuted that claim.
rows.anchor: أشار سبحانه بالتعرض لهذه القصة ونقل ما من صحف إبراهيم وموسى عليهما السلام إلى بيان وجه الحق فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage establishes that creation and governance belong to God and lead to a second life of recompense, which entails revealed religion and duties; the destruction of Noah’s, ‘Ad’s, Thamud’s, and the overturned cities’ peoples is evidence.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الخلق والتدبير لله سبحانه، إليه ينتهي كل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After these scriptural teachings, the surah warns that this warner belongs to the earlier warners, says the Hour is near, and ends by commanding prostration and worship.
rows.anchor: ثم عقب سبحانه هذا الذي نقله عن صحف النبيين الكريمين بالتنبيه على أن هذا النذير من النذر الأولى الخالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here turning away means turning away from spending in God’s cause, as the next verse clarifies.
rows.anchor: التولي هو الإعراض والمراد به بقرينة الآية التالية الإعراض عن الإنفاق في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving means spending, while ikda means cutting off the giving; the person gave a little and then held back firmly.
rows.anchor: والإعطاء الإنفاق والإكداء قطع العطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed fa in ‘Have you seen?’ branches the question from the preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: والتفريع الذي في قوله { أفرأيت } مبني على ما قدمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks the listener to consider someone who abandoned spending, gave a small amount, then stopped giving altogether.
rows.anchor: والمعنى فأخبرني عمن أعرض عن الإنفاق وأعطى قليلا من المال وأمسك بعد ذلك أشد الإمساك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns refer to the person who turned away, and the question is a repudiation.
rows.anchor: الضمائر لمن تولى والاستفهام للإنكار

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The reported interpretation asks whether he knows the unseen well enough to know that his companion will bear his sins and suffer punishment in his place if he deserves it.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام للإنكار والمعنى أيعلم الغيب فيترتب عليه أن يعلم أن صاحبه يتحمل عنه ذنوبه ويعذب مكانه يوم القيامة لو استحق العذاب. كذا فسروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai instead takes the unseen to mean the future course of worldly life: did he know that continued spending would exhaust his wealth and leave him poor?
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد نفي علمه بما غاب عنه من مستقبل حاله في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that someone else will carry his sins is addressed by the next statement that no bearer carries another’s burden.
rows.anchor: وأما تحمل الذنوب والعذاب فالمتعرض له قوله الآتي { أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls of Moses are the Torah.
rows.anchor: صحف موسى التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls of Abraham are the revelation sent down to him; their plural form indicates the many parts of that scripture.
rows.anchor: وصحف إبراهيم ما نزل عليه من الكتاب والجمع للإشارة إلى كثرته بكثرة أجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s fulfillment means that he fully and perfectly discharged his duty of servitude.
rows.anchor: وتوفيته عليه السلام تأديته ما عليه من الحق في العبودية أتم التأدية وأبلغها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about Abraham fulfilling his duty is illustrated by the verse saying he completed the trials imposed by his Lord.
rows.anchor: وإذ ابتلى إبراهيم ربه بكلمات فأتمهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although earlier Qur’an passages do not label these teachings as excerpts from the two scrolls, they present them as wisdom, admonitions, stories, and lessons; the question means whether he was told these scriptural teachings.
rows.anchor: فمعنى الآيتين أم لم ينبأ بهذه الأمور وهي في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wizr means a burden and is commonly used for sin; a bearing soul is one disposed to carry sin.
rows.anchor: الوزر الثقل وكثر استعماله في الإثم، والوازرة النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse states what is in Abraham’s and Moses’ scriptures: no soul is charged with another soul’s sin or held accountable for it.
rows.anchor: لا تحمل نفس إثم نفس أخرى أي لا تتأثم نفس بما لنفس أخرى من الإثم فلا تؤاخذ نفس بإثم نفس أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse and the following scriptural statements introduced by ‘that’ belong to the set of seventeen verses drawn from the two scriptures.
rows.anchor: وكذا سائر الآيات المصدرة بأن وأن إلى تمام سبع عشرة آية

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says sa‘y literally means brisk walking, less than running, and is used metaphorically for earnest effort in good or evil.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب السعي المشي السريع وهو دون العدو، ويستعمل للجد في الأمر خيرا كان أو شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām of ‘for the human being’ denotes true ownership: a lasting possession whose effects remain with its owner.
rows.anchor: ومعنى اللام في قوله { للإنسان } الملك الحقيقي الذي يقوم بصاحبه قياما باقيا ببقائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly wealth, children, status, and ornaments are only conventional possessions that leave a person at death; truly beneficial or harmful property is what one earns through one’s own good or bad work, not another’s deeds.
rows.anchor: فكل ذلك من الملك الاعتباري الوهمي الذي يصاحب الإنسان ما دام في دار الغرور

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier discussions of the verse are connected to the record of people’s deeds and their traces, concern for descendants, and God’s distinguishing the bad from the good.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في تفسير قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The effort is the person’s deeds, which will be seen on Judgment Day; the recompense context makes the timing clear, as in verses where deeds are made present and seen.
rows.anchor: المراد بالسعي ما سعى فيه من العمل وبالرؤية المشاهدة وظرف المشاهدة يوم القيامة بدليل تعقيبه بالجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive ‘will be seen’ suggests that someone besides the deed’s performer will observe it.
rows.anchor: لا يخلو من إشعار بأن هناك من يشاهد العمل غير عامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafa means completeness, since a complete thing fulfills all its required qualities; the fullest recompense is the most complete reward.
rows.anchor: الوفاء بمعنى التمام لأن الشيء التام يفي بجميع ما يطلب من صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to striving, meaning the person is repaid for his work with the fullest recompense.
rows.anchor: وضمير { يجزاه } للسعي الذي هو العمل والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muntaha is an infinitive noun meaning ending; stated absolutely, it conveys every kind of ending.
rows.anchor: المنتهى مصدر ميمي بمعنى الانتهاء وقد أطلق إطلاقا فيفيد مطلق الانتهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All beings and their effects, as well as every system of governance, ultimately depend on God, directly or through causes; God creates beings and the relations among them.
rows.anchor: فما في الوجود من شيء موجود إلا وينتهي في وجوده وآثار وجوده إلى الله سبحانه بلا واسطة أو مع الواسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes God’s absolute lordship: all governance ends with Him, including both the origin of things through creation and their return through resurrection.
rows.anchor: والآية تثبت الربوبية المطلقة لله سبحانه بإنهاء كل تدبير وكل التدبير إليه وتشمل انتهاء الأشياء إليه من حيث البدء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The restricted interpretation that the verse means only the creation’s return to God on Judgment Day is too narrow.
rows.anchor: يظهر ضعف ما قيل في تفسير الآية إن المراد بذلك رجوع الخلق إليه سبحانه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The interpretation that the final destination is only God’s reward and punishment unnecessarily restricts the verse.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما قيل إن المعنى أن إلى ثواب ربك وعقابه آخر الأمر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The interpretation that people’s endpoint is only God’s reckoning is too restrictive.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما قيل المعنى أن إلى حساب ربك منتهاهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The interpretation that thought terminates and stops before God also narrows the verse without textual restriction.
rows.anchor: وكذا ما قيل إليه سبحانه ينتهي الأفكار وتقف دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next twelve verses exemplify how creation and governance terminate in God; their exclusive phrasing establishes His sole lordship without a partner.
rows.anchor: الآية وما يتلوها إلى تمام اثنتي عشرة آية بيان لموارد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exclusive divine causation does not rule out natural or non-natural intermediaries such as human joy, organs of laughter, angels, or other causes; these are subject to God and not independent.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي ما في هذه الموارد من الحصر توسط أسباب أخر طبيعية أو غير طبيعية فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone brings laughter into the laugher and weeping into the weeper; human beings still perform and bear these acts, so both attributions are true in different senses.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى هو أوجد الضحك في الضاحك وأوجد البكاء في الباكي لا غيره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine will concerns laughter precisely as a voluntary human act; human choice causes it within God’s will, not alongside it, avoiding both fatalism and the Mu‘tazilite denial of God’s agency.
rows.anchor: فإرادة الإنسان سبب لضحكه في طول إرادة الله سبحانه لا في عرضها حتى تتزاحما ولا تجتمعا معا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The author rejects the gloss that God created only the capacities for laughter and weeping.
rows.anchor: يظهر فساد قول بعضهم إن معنى الآية أنه خلق قوتي الضحك والبكاء

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: The author rejects the gloss that the verse means God created joy and sorrow.
rows.anchor: وقول آخرين إن المعنى أنه خلق السرور والحزن

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: The author rejects the figurative reading that God makes the earth laugh with plants and the sky weep with rain.
rows.anchor: وقول آخرين إن المعنى أنه أضحك الأرض بالنبات وأبكى السماء بالمطر

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: The author rejects the gloss that God makes the people of Paradise laugh and the people of Hell weep.
rows.anchor: وقول آخرين إن المعنى أنه أضحك أهل الجنة وأبكى أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with laughter and weeping, death and life may have natural or non-natural intermediaries, including angels, while their creation remains exclusively God’s.
rows.anchor: الكلام في انتساب الموت والحياة إلى أسباب أخر طبيعية وغير طبيعية كالملائكة كالكلام في انتساب الضحك والبكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two spouses are male and female; nutfah is the male and female fluid from which a child is created, and amna means that a man poured out semen.
rows.anchor: النطفة ماء الرجل والمرأة الذي يخلق منه الولد، وأمنى الرجل أي صب المني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported alternative takes the verb to mean determination or measuring.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘male and female’ is an explanation of the two members of the pair.
rows.anchor: وقوله { الذكر والأنثى } بيان للزوجين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation for omitting the repeated pronoun is that creating the pair cannot be attributed to anyone besides God.
rows.anchor: قيل لم يذكر الضمير في الآية على طرز ما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second creation is the afterlife, where recompense takes place; its being incumbent on God means it is His irrevocable decree and promise, which He has said He will not break.
rows.anchor: النشأة الأخرى الخلقة الأخرى الثانية وهي الدار الآخرة التي فيها جزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aghna means that God gave wealth or sufficiency, while aqna means that He gave lasting possessions such as a house, garden, or livestock; mentioning the particular after the general honors it.
rows.anchor: أي أعطى الغنى وأعطى القنية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported alternative defines enriching as providing funds and aqna as making the recipient content with them.
rows.anchor: وقيل الإغناء التمويل والإقناء الإرضاء بذلك

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the phrase means that God makes people rich and poor.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم معنى الآية أنه هو أغنى وأفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shi‘ra is probably the Southern Dog Star, a bright fixed star east of Orion.
rows.anchor: كأن المراد بالشعرى الشعرى اليمانية وهي كوكبة مضيئة من الثوابت شرقي صورة الجبار في السماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is reported that Khuza‘a and Himyar worshiped the star; Abu Kabsha, a maternal ancestor of the Prophet, was among its worshipers.
rows.anchor: قيل كانت الخزاعة وحمير تعبد هذه الكوكبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abu Kabsha differed from his people in religion, the polytheists called the Prophet ‘son of Abu Kabsha’ for his own religious opposition to them.
rows.anchor: وكان المشركون يسمونه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ابن أبي كبشة لمخالفته إياهم في الدين

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: رواية غير مسماة
rows.claim: An unnamed report says the deceased knows a deed was done for him; even for a nāṣib it gives some benefit by lightening his burden.
rows.anchor: قلت وإن كان ناصبا ينفعه ذلك؟ قال نعم يخفف عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding report concerns gifting the reward of a deed, not performing the deed as a proxy for the deceased.
rows.anchor: مورد الرواية إهداء ثواب العمل دون العمل نيابة عن الميت

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet reports that God tells the angel assigned to a believer to record during illness the deeds that were recorded in health, since God has placed the believer in His care.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سنان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq says three rewards continue after death: ongoing charity, a rightly guided practice followed by others, and a righteous child’s prayer for the deceased.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال ليس يتبع الرجل بعد موته من الأجر إلا ثلاث خصال صدقة أجراها في حياته

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports, along with many similar reports from the Imams, broaden the meaning of a person’s striving to include deeds whose reward or effects continue through others.
rows.anchor: أقول وهذه الروايات الثلاث - وفي معناها روايات كثيرة جدا عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq cites the verse and instructs that when speech reaches God, one should stop.
rows.anchor: قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai regards the report as an expanded application of the word ‘ending.’
rows.anchor: أقول وهو من التوسعة في معنى الانتهاء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Baqir warns Ziyad that disputation breeds doubt, cancels deeds, and ruins its practitioner; people who pursued forbidden knowledge became confused, with another version saying they wandered on earth.
rows.anchor: إلى أبي عبيدة الحذاء قال قال أبو جعفر عليه السلام يا زياد إياك والخصومات

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr transmits the Prophet’s instruction to contemplate God’s creation, not God Himself, lest one perish.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many reports in both traditions forbidding thought about God are guidance for those unprepared for difficult rational inquiry, whose delving into it risks lasting ruin.
rows.anchor: والنهي إرشادي متعلق بمن لا يحسن الورود في المسائل العقلية العميقة فيكون خوضه فيها تعرضا للهلاك الدائم

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi says God made the sky weep through rain and the earth laugh through vegetation.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { وأنه هو أضحك وأبكى } قال أبكى السماء بالمطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai treats this report as an extended figurative use of making weep and laugh.
rows.anchor: أقول هو من التوسعة في معنى الإبكاء والإضحاك

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam Ali explains that God provides every person a livelihood and makes the person content with what his hands earn.
rows.anchor: قال قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { وأنه هو أغنى وأقنى }
